paragraphs: Disentanglement concerns separating the factors that account for variation in data. Researchers have formalized this idea in many ways, making it difficult to tell whether two definitions describe the same property or impose different requirements. This paper examines those definitions together, using category theory to give their comparison a shared mathematical language.

The authors propose cartesian and monoidal products as central concepts for describing disentanglement. These provide ways to express how separate components combine into a larger structure. The analysis then distinguishes four settings: functions, equivariant maps, relations, and stochastic maps. Examining each setting within the same framework exposes both common structure and consequential differences between formulations.

The contribution is conceptual: it clarifies what different definitions commit a researcher to when describing a representation as disentangled. The authors argue that this comparison can help researchers choose a definition suited to their context. Their proposal supplies a framework for navigating existing formulations rather than establishing one universally appropriate definition for every application.
icml-2023-a-category-theoretical-meta-an.tldr: A category-theoretic framework clarifies the shared structure and important differences among definitions of disentanglement.

paragraphs: Models trained on one distribution can struggle when deployed on another. AdaNPC addresses this problem by adapting its prediction memory as test examples arrive. The motivation is to exploit information from the target domain without requiring offline access to target data or sophisticated optimization procedures during inference.

The method begins with a memory of training examples represented by their features and labels. For a new example, it retrieves the k closest stored examples and uses their votes to predict a label. It then stores the new example’s features together with that predicted label. Repeating this process gradually shifts the memory toward the test distribution, with little additional computation.

The paper provides theoretical justification and reports substantial improvements over competitive methods on domain generalization benchmarks. For adaptation across a sequence of domains, it reports accuracy 50% higher than advanced test-time adaptation methods. This is a reported comparison in that setting, not a percentage-point claim. The central result is that updating a memory can provide effective adaptation without a complicated inference-time optimization procedure.
icml-2023-adanpc-exploring-non-parametri.tldr: AdaNPC adapts to incoming data by predicting from nearby stored examples and adding its predictions to memory.

paragraphs: Code generation systems can sample several candidate programs and rank them using the probability assigned by a language model. However, that ranking can favor degenerate solutions. This paper introduces Coder-Reviewer reranking, which evaluates candidates from two directions to improve the choice among programs that have already been generated.

The Coder scores a program given the user’s instruction. The Reviewer evaluates how likely that instruction is given the program. Combining these perspectives adds a check on whether a candidate program supports the requested description. The approach can be implemented through prompting, works across programming languages, and performs well with readily available hyperparameter settings.

The evaluation covers six datasets and eight models from three model families. The authors report consistent, significant improvements over ranking with the Coder alone, reaching an absolute accuracy gain of up to 17%. When paired with filtering for executability, the approach often outperforms minimum Bayes risk reranking. These findings support using the reverse instruction-given-program score as a useful complement to the usual generation score.
icml-2023-coder-reviewer-reranking-for-c.tldr: Ranking generated programs with both code-given-instruction and instruction-given-code scores improves code selection in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Neural networks can model how a dynamical system changes over time while failing to respect quantities that should remain constant. ConCerNet addresses this mismatch by learning conservation properties from observed trajectories and then incorporating those properties into the dynamics model. Its aim is to make predictions both accurate and consistent with learned invariants.

The framework has two stages. A contrastive learning method first extracts invariants from trajectory observations. A neural projection layer then ensures that the learned dynamics preserve those learned quantities. The authors also prove a functional relationship between the learned representation and the system’s unknown invariant function, giving theoretical support to the discovery stage.

Experiments show large, consistent improvements over baseline neural networks in coordinate error and conservation measures. The preservation guarantee concerns the learned invariants, while the theoretical relationship connects their representation to the unknown system invariant. The method does not depend on prior knowledge of conservation laws, and the authors describe how an autoencoder can extend its neural parameterization to complex, large-scale dynamics.
icml-2023-concernet-a-contrastive-learni.tldr: ConCerNet learns conservation properties from trajectories and constrains neural dynamics models to preserve the learned invariants.

paragraphs: A link-stealing attack tries to determine whether an edge was present in the graph used to train a graph neural network. This paper investigates whether different groups of edges face different levels of exposure. That question matters because an overall attack score can leave substantial differences in privacy risk between groups unexamined.

The authors provide theoretical evidence that vulnerability to link stealing is uneven across edge groups. They also develop an attack approach that customizes its strategy for different groups. This connects the theoretical observation to a practical consequence: an attacker can exploit those differences instead of applying the same strategy to every edge.

Experiments on nine real-world datasets reveal clear disparities. One reported example is an approximately 25% difference in attack AUC between groups in the Credit graph. The group-based approach also outperforms existing attack methods in the evaluation. Together, these findings show that unequal exposure is both measurable and useful to attackers, making group differences relevant to assessing graph privacy.
icml-2023-demystifying-uneven-vulnerabil.tldr: The paper shows that edge groups face unequal link-stealing risks and that attackers can exploit those differences.

paragraphs: A fake-audio detector can perform well on one dataset and deteriorate on another. Updating it for new data also raises the problem of catastrophic forgetting: learning the new dataset can erode previously acquired knowledge. This paper proposes Regularized Adaptive Weight Modification, or RAWM, to improve adaptation while retaining earlier detection capabilities.

RAWM adjusts the direction of weight updates according to the proportion of genuine and fake utterances during fine-tuning. This addresses a limitation of orthogonal weight modification, which does not account for similarities in genuine audio across datasets. The adaptive direction is designed to support learning about new fake audio while preserving knowledge from the previous model.

The method also adds a regularization constraint to retain the earlier feature distribution when genuine audio comes from substantially different acoustic conditions. Across multiple datasets, the authors report significant improvements in cross-dataset experiments. The two components address related sources of forgetting: changes in how the detector learns and shifts in genuine-audio features. The authors also describe applicability to related areas such as speech emotion recognition.
icml-2023-do-you-remember-overcoming-cat.tldr: RAWM combines adaptive weight updates and distribution-preserving regularization to reduce forgetting when fake-audio detectors learn new datasets.

paragraphs: Bayesian inference supports learning and reasoning under uncertainty, but applications can involve sensitive data. This paper studies how to give Metropolis-Hastings, a fundamental sampling method, differential privacy guarantees while keeping it practical for large datasets. The challenge is that privacy protection in existing sampling methods often comes at the expense of accuracy and computational efficiency.

The proposed DP-Fast MH algorithm is described as exact and fast, while examining only a minibatch of data in most iterations. The qualification matters: the approach does not claim to use a minibatch on every iteration. Its contribution combines private inference with reduced data access during much of the sampling process.

The authors also establish a theoretical trade-off among privacy, batch size, and convergence rate. This explains how stronger privacy requirements interact with scalability and the speed of inference, rather than treating these as independent design choices. Experiments support the algorithm’s effectiveness and efficiency. Together, the algorithm and analysis clarify how private Bayesian sampling can remain accurate while managing computational costs.
icml-2023-dp-fast-mh-private-fast-and-ac.tldr: DP-Fast MH provides exact private Metropolis-Hastings sampling and characterizes the trade-off between privacy, batch size, and convergence.

paragraphs: Bayesian optimization becomes challenging when the search space has many dimensions or the objective behaves differently across regions. Existing approaches for these settings can require extensive hyperparameter tuning. BALLET addresses this difficulty by adaptively identifying a promising part of the search space and directing optimization toward that region.

The framework uses two probabilistic models with different jobs. A coarse Gaussian process identifies a high-confidence region of interest through a superlevel set, meaning a region selected according to a modeled level threshold. A localized Gaussian process then handles optimization inside that region. This separates the problem of deciding where to search from the problem of choosing evaluations within the selected area.

The theoretical analysis shows that BALLET can efficiently reduce the search space and can obtain a tighter regret bound than standard Bayesian optimization without filtering. This is a possible advantage established by the analysis, rather than an unconditional improvement. Experiments on synthetic and real-world tasks support its effectiveness, while the framework is described as easy to tune and compatible with existing local optimization methods.
icml-2023-learning-regions-of-interest-f.tldr: BALLET uses a coarse model to find promising regions and a local model to focus Bayesian optimization within them.

paragraphs: Bias amplification occurs when a model’s test-time behavior strengthens biases already present in its training data. Existing measures typically examine individual annotated attributes. This paper argues that such measurements can miss biases involving combinations of attributes, even though many datasets label each example with several attributes at once.

The authors demonstrate that models can exploit correlations involving multiple attributes. They also identify a separate measurement problem: positive and negative bias scores can cancel when aggregated, making amplification appear small or absent. Existing metrics additionally lack a clear ideal value, which makes their results harder to interpret. These issues motivate the proposed Multi-Attribute Bias Amplification metric.

The paper evaluates the metric through analyses of COCO, imSitu, and CelebA, and uses it to benchmark bias mitigation methods. Its contribution is a way to examine amplification that single-attribute summaries can overlook. The findings also suggest directions for improving mitigation efforts by evaluating them against a broader account of the correlations models learn.
icml-2023-men-also-do-laundry-multi-attr.tldr: A multi-attribute metric reveals bias amplification that individual-attribute measurements and canceling aggregate scores can hide.

paragraphs: Online allocation requires making decisions as requests arrive while trying to maximize total revenue. This paper considers resources with both minimum and maximum consumption requirements. The lower bounds complicate decisions because conserving resources is not enough: the final allocation must also consume enough of each constrained resource.

The authors introduce a feasibility measure, xi*, that captures how difficult the constrained problem is, together with an optimization procedure for estimating it with theoretical guarantees. Their online algorithm uses that information to initialize threshold prices. It then updates those prices dynamically and uses them to decide how to handle each incoming request.

The analysis gives high-probability competitive guarantees whose error terms scale as epsilon divided by xi* minus epsilon when feasibility is known, and epsilon divided by xi* minus the square root of epsilon when it is unknown. Thus, the guarantees depend on the feasibility measure and these denominators. The result establishes nearly optimal performance together with a high probability of satisfying both sides of the resource constraints.
icml-2023-nearly-optimal-competitive-rat.tldr: An adaptive pricing algorithm achieves nearly optimal online allocation guarantees that depend on feasibility under lower and upper resource bounds.

paragraphs: Deep kernel learning combines deep learning with kernel methods, but understanding its generalization requires accounting for an implicit nonlinear mapping. The paper explains that this mapping prevents existing capacity-based analyses for deep learning from applying directly. It develops a different analysis to address that gap in the theory.

The approach uses the way function classes compose to derive bounds on the capacity of deep kernel models. Its main results are nearly tight generalization bounds based on uniform covering numbers and Rademacher chaos complexity. These are mathematical tools for characterizing the richness of the functions a model can represent, and the resulting bounds have only mild dependence on depth.

For some common function classes, the authors further estimate these quantities using pseudo-dimensions and kernel pseudo-dimensions. This makes the general framework more concrete for those classes. The results provide theoretical guarantees without strong assumptions and partially explain why deep learning combined with kernels can generalize well. The claim is a partial theoretical explanation, rather than a complete account of empirical performance.
icml-2023-nearly-tight-bounds-for-deep-k.tldr: The paper derives nearly tight generalization bounds for deep kernel models with mild dependence on network depth.

paragraphs: Test-time adaptation updates a model to cope with distribution changes encountered during deployment. Comparing methods has been difficult because studies use inconsistent experimental conditions. This paper introduces TTAB, an open benchmark containing nine leading algorithms, diverse distribution shifts, and two evaluation protocols, to make those comparisons more systematic.

The experiments identify three recurring problems. Hyperparameter choice, especially model selection, becomes difficult because online batches depend on one another. Adaptation performance also varies substantially with the quality of the starting model. Finally, some kinds of distribution shift remain difficult for existing methods even when algorithmic conditions are optimal.

These findings mean that an adaptation result needs to be interpreted alongside the starting model, the shift being tested, and the evaluation setup. The authors call for clearer reporting of experimental conditions and broader testing across models and shifts. They also argue for revisiting the assumptions behind successful practical adaptation. TTAB supplies an evaluation framework for examining those dependencies rather than assuming adaptation will reliably help across settings.
icml-2023-on-pitfalls-of-test-time-adapt.tldr: TTAB reveals that test-time adaptation depends strongly on model quality, evaluation conditions, and the type of distribution shift.

paragraphs: SARSA is an on-policy reinforcement learning algorithm that can oscillate within a bounded region when used with linear function approximation. This behavior, called chattering, differs from settling at a single fixed point. The paper investigates two unresolved questions: how quickly the algorithm approaches that region and how large the region can be.

The analysis establishes a convergence rate for projected SARSA to a bounded region. Projection restricts the algorithm to a prescribed region, but the authors show that its eventual region can be much smaller than that imposed boundary. This stronger conclusion requires that the magnitude of the rewards is not too large.

Earlier fixed-point convergence analyses require a sufficiently small Lipschitz constant for the policy improvement operator. The new analysis permits arbitrary Lipschitz constants, extending the range of behavior that theory can characterize. Its guarantee concerns reaching a bounded region, not convergence to one point. That distinction lets the analysis describe chattering while quantifying the approach to the region in which it occurs.
icml-2023-on-the-convergence-of-sarsa-wi.tldr: The paper bounds how quickly projected linear SARSA reaches a bounded region without requiring a small policy-improvement Lipschitz constant.

paragraphs: Multimodal contrastive learning builds representations from paired data such as images and text. Although it performs well on visual tasks, its advantage over self-supervised contrastive learning has lacked a clear theoretical explanation. This paper connects multimodal contrastive learning to asymmetric matrix factorization and uses that connection to establish generalization guarantees for downstream visual tasks.

The analysis also relates the two learning approaches directly. It shows that multimodal contrastive learning implicitly performs self-supervised contrastive learning using pseudo-positive pairs induced by text pairs. Through this perspective, text influences which visual examples are treated as related during representation learning, giving a concrete role to the additional modality.

The authors characterize the advantage as positive pairs that are more semantically consistent and more diverse. Their analysis shows that these properties benefit downstream generalization. Motivated by this result, they propose methods that use multimodal information to improve self-supervised contrastive learning and report significant gains on ImageNet. The work therefore links a theoretical explanation of pair quality to practical changes in representation training.
icml-2023-on-the-generalization-of-multi.tldr: The analysis explains how text-induced positive pairs can improve visual contrastive learning through semantic consistency and diversity.

paragraphs: Creating useful features can substantially improve learning from tabular data, but manually developing them takes expert effort. Automated methods face a large search problem: they must distinguish helpful features from a vast collection of candidates. OpenFE addresses both the quality of that selection and the computational work needed to make it.

The tool combines two components. A feature boosting method evaluates the additional predictive benefit of candidate features. A two-stage pruning procedure then narrows the candidate pool from a coarse assessment to a more detailed one. Together, these components aim to retain useful features while making the search efficient enough to be practical.

On ten benchmark datasets, the authors report large improvements over existing methods. In two Kaggle competitions, OpenFE features paired with a simple baseline model outperform 99.3% and 99.6% of participating teams, respectively. These results support the claimed competitiveness with expert feature generation in the evaluated settings. The paper also gives a theoretical perspective showing that feature generation can help in a simple, representative setting.
icml-2023-openfe-automated-feature-gener.tldr: OpenFE efficiently evaluates and prunes candidate features, achieving strong tabular-learning results against baselines and competition participants.

paragraphs: Reward-free reinforcement learning separates exploration from planning. An agent first collects experience without observing rewards, then receives a reward function and must use that experience to find a good policy. This paper addresses the high exploration cost of long planning horizons for linear mixture Markov decision processes, whose transitions are linear combinations of known feature mappings.

The algorithm combines uncertainty-weighted regression, a pseudo-reward that drives exploration, and a high-order moment estimator. Its uncertainty estimates account for both randomness in the environment and uncertainty arising from incomplete knowledge. These components guide data collection before the eventual reward function is available, supporting later planning from the collected samples.

When total reward is bounded by one, the required number of exploration episodes scales as d squared divided by epsilon squared, up to logarithmic factors. Here d is feature dimension and epsilon specifies policy accuracy. Horizon dependence is only polylogarithmic, which is the sense of “horizon-free.” A matching lower bound up to logarithmic factors establishes near-optimal sample complexity in this setting.
icml-2023-optimal-horizon-free-reward-fr.tldr: For linear mixture MDPs with total reward bounded by one, the algorithm achieves nearly optimal reward-free exploration with only polylogarithmic horizon dependence.

paragraphs: Dense visual tasks such as detection and segmentation need representations that preserve localized information. Contrastive learning at the pixel or patch level can support this, but matching corresponding locations across two views is difficult. Feeding the same view twice simplifies alignment, yet reduces input variation and can hurt learning performance.

The paper proposes Positional Query for patch-level Contrastive Learning, or PQCL, as a plug-in method. Positional queries enable patch-level comparisons between two views with exact correspondence. They also increase input variation to strengthen training. The method therefore addresses both the matching problem and the reduced diversity associated with simply repeating an identical view.

The authors apply PQCL to the transformer-based DINO and iBOT frameworks and evaluate classification, detection, and segmentation. They report consistent improvements, particularly for dense prediction, and state-of-the-art results in most evaluated settings. These findings support the value of combining reliable patch correspondence with varied inputs when pretraining visual representations, especially when later tasks depend on understanding specific parts of an image.
icml-2023-patch-level-contrastive-learni.tldr: PQCL uses positional queries to combine exact patch correspondence with varied inputs, improving visual pretraining in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Combining multiple data modalities requires capturing their relationships while managing differences in quality. Low-quality inputs can interfere with useful information from other modalities. Dynamic fusion offers a way to adapt how modalities interact, but the paper identifies a shortage of theoretical explanations for why such approaches should be robust.

The authors study a widely used multimodal fusion framework through generalization theory. Their analysis reveals that several uncertainty estimation approaches can support robust fusion. This provides a theoretical basis for using uncertainty when combining modalities, connecting the fusion decision to the challenge of handling uneven input quality.

Building on that analysis, the paper proposes Quality-aware Multimodal Fusion, or QMF. The framework is intended to improve classification accuracy and robustness by accounting for quality during fusion. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks support the findings. The contribution combines an analysis within the studied fusion framework with an evaluated method, giving both theoretical motivation and empirical support for quality-aware multimodal learning.
icml-2023-provable-dynamic-fusion-for-lo.tldr: QMF uses uncertainty-informed, quality-aware fusion to improve multimodal classification and robustness, supported by theory and benchmark experiments.

paragraphs: Diffusion models can generate high-quality data, but their many sampling iterations make inference slow. ReDi accelerates generation by reusing information from previously computed sampling trajectories. Its retrieval-based approach does not require learning an additional acceleration mechanism, although it does rely on a precomputed knowledge base.

Early in generation, ReDi compares the partially generated trajectory with trajectories in that knowledge base. It retrieves a similar one, skips a substantial stretch of intermediate sampling steps, and resumes from a later point along the retrieved trajectory. The key idea is to use a relevant stored continuation to avoid computing every intermediate step anew.

The authors provide a theoretical guarantee for generation performance and report a twofold inference speedup in experiments. They also find that ReDi generalizes well to zero-shot image generation across domains, including image stylization. These findings support trajectory retrieval as a practical route to faster diffusion sampling, with the reported efficiency gain coming from bypassing steps rather than executing the full sampling process.
icml-2023-redi-efficient-learning-free-d.tldr: ReDi retrieves stored diffusion trajectories to skip intermediate sampling steps, delivering a reported twofold inference speedup without additional learning.

paragraphs: Structured variational autoencoders combine graphical-model structure for latent variables with neural networks that connect those variables to observations. They are appealing for sequences because the prior can express temporal dependencies. Despite this design, implementation difficulties have encouraged the use of more general alternatives. This paper revisits whether modern tools can make the structured approach more practical.

The authors develop an implementation of the underlying message-passing algorithms that supports hardware acceleration, parallel execution, and automatic differentiation. This directly addresses the computational and implementation demands of exploiting latent structure. They then show that using structure in the prior produces more accurate models and posterior distributions, with corresponding gains on prediction tasks.

The work also demonstrates how these models naturally handle missing observations and uses that capability to build a self-supervised training method. Across the reported comparisons, structured variational autoencoders offer advantages in accuracy and efficiency over more general alternatives. The findings connect better implementation with the statistical benefits of preserving useful structure in the latent model.
icml-2023-revisiting-structured-variatio.tldr: Modern implementations make structured variational autoencoders practical while retaining accuracy, efficiency, and missing-data advantages from their latent structure.

paragraphs: Some parts of an environment’s state evolve independently of the agent’s actions. The paper calls these contexts, with examples including customer demand and the speed of a lead car. Changes in how contexts evolve between training and deployment can degrade reinforcement learning performance, even though the agent does not control those changes.

The proposed robust situational Markov decision process explicitly models possible deviations in context transitions. This focuses robustness on the source of disturbance identified by the problem. To handle large context spaces, the authors introduce a softmin-smoothed robust Bellman operator that approximately learns robust Q-values. They incorporate this framework into the SAC reinforcement learning algorithm.

Experiments cover robot control with changing contexts and inventory control. The authors report better generalization, greater robustness to deviations in context transitions, and improvements over existing robust reinforcement learning methods. These results support explicitly representing action-independent disturbances when designing robust policies. The approximation in the value-learning operator is part of the approach used to make that framework scalable.
icml-2023-robust-situational-reinforceme.tldr: The RS-MDP framework improves robustness by explicitly modeling disturbances in context variables that evolve independently of an agent’s actions.

paragraphs: Training neural networks requires memory for intermediate activations. Rockmate automatically transforms PyTorch model code into an equivalent model that respects a specified activation-memory budget by recomputing some intermediate results. This gives users a way to trade additional computation for reduced memory use without manually organizing the recomputation strategy.

The tool detects computational and data dependencies and represents the model as a sequence of complex blocks. It adapts Checkmate within individual blocks and Rotor across the sequence. This division combines an approach that handles general dependencies with one that is fast for sequential structures. The authors identify this block structure in several model families, including Transformers, ResNet, and RegNets.

Experiments across many models find Rockmate as fast as Rotor and as efficient as Checkmate. In many cases, activation memory falls by a factor of two to five, with overhead around 10% to 20%. These are measured trade-offs rather than universal savings. The results show how recognizing model structure can make automatic recomputation both efficient to plan and useful during training.
icml-2023-rockmate-an-efficient-fast-aut.tldr: Rockmate automatically plans activation recomputation in PyTorch, substantially reducing memory with modest overhead in many tested models.

paragraphs: Persistence diagrams are used in topological data analysis to describe structure in point clouds. The paper addresses two problems with existing construction methods: sensitivity to noise and to differences in how densely points are distributed. Both can make the resulting representation less useful when the observed point cloud is uneven or noisy.

The authors first analyze the properties an approach needs to address these two issues together. They then propose a filter function based on a new data-dependent kernel that has those properties. The contribution connects the construction of the representation to explicit requirements for handling noise and varied density, rather than treating the downstream task alone as the design objective.

The empirical evaluation compares the proposed filter with three existing topological data analysis methods. It yields better results for t-SNE visualization and SVM classification in those comparisons. These findings support the usefulness of the proposed construction for both visual exploration and predictive analysis. The evidence combines a property-based design argument with downstream tests of the resulting representation.
icml-2023-towards-a-persistence-diagram-.tldr: A data-dependent kernel yields a topological filter designed for noise and varied density, improving the reported visualization and classification results.

paragraphs: Text rationalization explains a prediction by selecting a subset of the input. Association-based methods can struggle when several snippets are strongly correlated and support similar predictive accuracy. In that situation, a selected snippet may appear useful without identifying the true rationale. This paper develops a causal approach to address that ambiguity.

The authors introduce a structural causal model of rationalization and use it to define probabilities of causation. They build the approach around two desired properties, non-spuriousness and efficiency, and establish theoretical identification results. Those results form the central basis for learning rationales that are necessary and sufficient within the proposed causal formulation.

Experiments on real-world review and medical datasets show superior performance compared with state-of-the-art methods. The contribution connects explanation selection to explicit causal quantities, giving the method a basis beyond predictive association alone. Its theoretical claims belong to the proposed structural model, while the experiments provide evidence that this formulation improves rationalization in the evaluated text settings.
icml-2023-towards-trustworthy-explanatio.tldr: A causal model of text rationalization helps identify necessary and sufficient explanations when correlated snippets make association-based selection ambiguous.

paragraphs: Slot attention is used to organize images and videos into object-centered representations. The paper identifies a limitation arising from its set-equivariance: it cannot break ties, which restricts its ability to handle videos whose number of objects changes. Addressing this assignment behavior is the central motivation for the proposed modification.

The authors first establish a connection between slot attention and optimal transport. They use that perspective to design MESH, short for Minimize Entropy of Sinkhorn, as a cross-attention module. The module combines the ability of unregularized optimal transport to break ties with the computational speed of regularized optimal transport, aiming to retain useful properties of both.

Slot attention equipped with MESH is evaluated on multiple object-centric learning benchmarks. The authors report significant improvements over ordinary slot attention in every evaluated setting. These findings support changing the attention assignment mechanism to overcome the identified tie-breaking limitation. The theoretical connection also gives a principled way to frame the change, linking the behavior of object assignments to the properties of optimal transport.
icml-2023-unlocking-slot-attention-by-ch.tldr: MESH uses an optimal-transport perspective to give slot attention efficient tie-breaking and improve object-centric learning across tested settings.
